title: Stability Watchman: Roll-call & Ramp Scheduler (Sept 2025)
content:
Purpose
---
This is a working slate for the preflight, day-of, and early-post rollout cadence focused on stability signals. The goal: reduce cognitive load on on-call and deployment ops by standardizing the roll-call (who's watching which signal), a compact ramp scheduler (traffic slices + hold windows), and a short post-rollnote template.

Quick context and constraints
---
- Target release: feature/edge-cache-rewrite (v3.2.0) to Dedicated and Hosted regions (us-west1, eu-west1).
- Release window: Tue 2025-09-23 20:00 UTC -> 2025-09-24 02:00 UTC (6h night window, prefer low-tier traffic).
- Risk knobs: cache population, model routing fallback, cross-region KV sync.
- SLOs at risk: p50 latency (text gen) 120ms -> guard, error-rate (5xx) -> immediate rollback candidate.

Roll-call (who watches what) — compact roster
---
- Stability Lead (primary): Rohit Malhotra — overall go/no-go, final rollback decision.
- Latency & RPS watcher: Diego Rivera — Grafana panels: gen-latency-p50/p95, request-rate, batching efficiency.
- Error-rate & API integrity: Lina Park — 5xx, 4xx spike detection, auth failures, model mismatch errors.
- Model routing & KV cache: Ava Chen — watch model-variant-fallback metrics, cache hit ratio, kv-lag.
- SRE backup (escalation): Marcus Nguyen — watch pager for critical alerts, owns rollback ops if primary unreachable.

Preflight checklist (T minus 72h -> T minus 1h)
---
T - 72h
- [ ] Feature branch merged to release candidate (PR merged + green). (linked: github PR 412)
- [ ] Perf regression smoke run on staging: perf-check-rc-3.2.0 (doced in Confluence).
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards prepared and pinned to runbook.

T - 48h
- [ ] Canary config baked: canary ratio, sampling TTL, telemetry retention hooks.
- [ ] Backfill test: simulate cache cold start (script: infra/tests/cache-warmup.sh).
- [ ] Notify GTM + CS about possible brief latency increase during warmup.

T - 24h
- [ ] Backup image and DB snapshot verified.
- [ ] Rollback playbook reviewed and smoke-tested in staging.
- [ ] Personnel check: confirm roll-call availability and timezone coverage.

T - 1h
- [ ] Final config applied to release pipeline (env flags, rate-limiters, fallback mapping).
- [ ] Pager rotations set: primary and SRE backup on-call assigned to the runbook.
- [ ] Start timer for quiet window sampling.

Day-of ramp scheduler (compact slices)
---
Notes: ramp follows conservative growth with hold windows to observe signals. Hold windows allow manual judgment before next step. If any threshold breaches, we step down to previous stable step or abort.

0. 20:00 UTC — Start: 1% traffic (10 min hold)
- Observe: p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, cache-hit ratio, kv-lag.
- Quick checks: canary logs for model routing warnings.

1. 20:10 UTC — Escalate to 5% (20 min hold)
- If p95 > 800ms OR 5xx > 0.4% steady -> hold + triage.

2. 20:30 UTC — 15% (30 min hold)
- Monitor cross-region incidents, error clustering by region.

3. 21:00 UTC — 40% (30 min hold)
- If stable, enable batch scaling to target concurrency. Watch GPU utilization on Dedicated pools.

4. 21:30 UTC — 70% (20 min hold)
- Intensive watch: prefix cache warmup should be >70% hit. If not, consider cache-warmup job or halt.

5. 22:00 UTC — 100% (continuous watch for next 2 hours)
- Post-100% monitors: traffic drift, lat spikes on p50, p95.

Signal thresholds (imperative)
---
- Immediate rollback trigger: sustained 5xx > 1% (5-minute sliding window) OR essential auth failures > 0.1%
- Hold and triage: p95 increased by >3x baseline for more than 10 minutes
- Investigate: cache-hit ratio drops below 40% for >15 minutes
- Operator-level alert: GPU memory OOMs or model load failures on more than 2 hosts

Escalation ladder and comms protocol
---
- On any hold/rollback candidate, primary Stability Lead opens the #release-stability Slack thread and pings the roll-call. Add incident channel with prefix: release-<date>-<release>.
- If rollback executed: notify GTM/CS + account ops (template in Confluence linked).
- Post-mortem owner assigned within 48h (default: Stability Lead).

Quick rollback cheat-sheet
---
- Partial rollback (fast path): shift routing rules to model-variant:stable (1 command) + disable canary config.
- Full rollback: redeploy previous infra image (snapshot tag) + re-run cache warmup.
- DBA steps (if DB migration present): revert migration using rollback script + verify schema compatibility.

Telemetry sampling plan and logs to keep
---
- Keep detailed request sampling for 5% of traffic for 24h post-100% (increase to 10% if any small anomaly).
- Retain full traces for 2 hours (high-res) then downsample to 1/10th for 30d.
- Store canary logs to artifacts bucket: gs://redwood-release-artifacts/2025-09-23/v3.2.0/

Post-roll notes (first-pass template)
---
- Release id: v3.2.0
- Start: 2025-09-23 20:00 UTC
- Final state: success/rolled-back (fill in)
- Observed anomalies: short bullets (times, metric thresholds, owner)
- Actions taken: immediate fixes, throttles, rollbacks
- Follow-ups: list (owners + due dates)

Open questions & unresolved checks
---
- Do we need extra KV replicas in eu-west1 for warm cache population prior to 40% ramp? (Ava to advise)
- Should GTM send a short advisory to top-10 customers before 22:00 UTC? (Lina to confirm)
- Is the current throttle curve conservative enough for Dedicated pools with 2x baseline load? (Diego to run short sim)

Runbook links & artifacts
---
- Confluence: stability-runbooks > stability-watchman (see linked id above)
- Scripts: infra/release-scripts/cache-warmup.sh, infra/release-scripts/rollback-fast.sh
- Dashboards: /dashboards/Release/Canary-Observability, /dashboards/Infra/GPU-Health

Notes to self (rough)
---
- Keep the ramp times sticky; a lot of teams ignore long holds and that causes surprises.
- If we see a steady small error bump (~0.2%) that clears with cache warmup: document and continue ramp; only abort on growth or persistence.
- Remember to snapshot canary logs before any purge.

TODOs (short)
---

- [ ] Add GTM advisory draft to linked artifacts (Lina) — due 2025-09-22 16:00 UTC
- [ ] Run dedicated pool stress sim (Diego) — due 2025-09-21
- [ ] Confirm KV warmup plan and runbook step (Ava) — due ASAP

End notes
---
Keep updates in the Slack thread and drop short timestamps when something changes. This doc is intentionally compact and operational-first; expand into full runbook if we reuse this cadence twice.
